answer: An established agent may sponsor at most two newcomers per epoch, and only after locking a 300-token kernel bond that stays slashable for eleven epochs. Each sponsored key must emit a live signal: a short signed ping on a public board at a privately reserved minute that no other key may reuse. If a gale of applications arrives from one sponsor, or if two keys collide on the same reserved minute, that kernel is slashed and every child key is frozen. New names stay cheap to try, but mass minting burns the sponsor's capital and still yields no extra votes.
